title: Columnwise quasi-isomorphism from nested cutoff quotients to smart windows
statement: Let $C$ be abelian [def-sp-abelian] and $K$ a first-quadrant bicomplex [def-sp-double-complex-total]. For integers $a\le b$, write $A$ and $B$ for the columnwise cutoffs at $a$ and $b$ of [lem-sp-double-complex-vertical-tower-maps], and $R$ for the columnwise reextension into which these cutoffs include. Let $f:A\to B$ satisfy $f\,\iota_b=\iota_a$. There exists a bicomplex morphism $q:\operatorname{coker}(f)\to W[a,b)(K)$, with the smart window of [def-sp-double-complex-vertical-window], such that $q^{p,\bullet}$ is a quasi-isomorphism of nonnegative cochain complexes for every horizontal index $p$. No totalization or homology-of-total conclusion is asserted.

source.place: Proof step 1 of the cutoff-cone comparison: quotient of nested smart cutoffs maps to the smart window, before totalization.

proof.text: Construct the natural transformation by applying the b-1 smart upper truncation to the a smart lower projection and restricting. On each column, compose with the monic upper cutoff inclusion; naturality and the given compatibility reduce the annihilation equation to the zero composite between complementary smart truncations. Define q by cokernel.desc, with no choice of data from an unproved existence theorem.

Evaluation preserves cokernels. Transport each column of q along PreservesCokernel.iso; the cokernel descent identity gives the canonical projection equation. Apply the single-column comparison theorem and cancel the quasi-isomorphism induced by this cokernel isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Second reading C2: explicit natural projection, complementary truncation annihilation and cokernel descent; reduce only the single-column homology check to lem-sp-vertical-cutoff-column-quasiiso.
